title: Promises
description: Promises represent eventual values — chain with .then, handle errors with .catch, run cleanup in .finally.

notes: Returning from .then becomes the next promise value; throwing inside .then becomes a rejection.
Without a .catch, an unhandled rejection just disappears (and warns in modern runtimes). Always terminate chains with .catch.
.finally is for cleanup — it does not receive the value or affect the resolved value.

questions.explain: It wraps the value rather than handing it back — you still need `.then` (or `await`) to read the `7` out, which is exactly what `doubleAsync` relies on in L3.

questions.q: A rejected Promise is handled by:
options: .then (rejections fall through to its single callback)
.finally (since it always runs, it can branch on rejection)
questions.explain: `.catch(fn)` is just `.then(undefined, fn)` — a rejection skips every fulfillment handler until it finds one. A surrounding `try/catch` never sees it, because the chain settles long after that block has exited.

questions.q: What does throwing inside a .then callback do?
options: Propagates synchronously to the surrounding try/catch around the .then call
Becomes a rejected Promise the next .catch handles
Resolves the chain with the Error as the fulfilled value
Skips the rest of the chain and triggers `unhandledrejection` immediately
questions.explain: The handler already runs in a microtask, so its throw can only settle the promise that `.then` returned — as rejected — and the next `.catch` downstream picks it up.

options: After the Promise settles, either way
questions.explain: It fires on fulfill and reject alike, receives no argument, and passes the original settlement through untouched — a rejection stays rejected after `.finally`.

exercises.prompt: Resolve immediately with 42 and log the value.

blanks.hint: runs after settle, no value passed

exercises.prompt: Catch a rejection and log "caught" plus the message.

blanks.hint: success branch — won't fire on reject

L3.prompt: Write `doubleAsync(x)` returning `Promise.resolve(x * 2)`. Call `doubleAsync(5)` and log the resolved value with .then.
hints: Promise.resolve(v) gives a Promise already fulfilled with v.
Use .then to receive the resolved value.
